name: Community Health Allied Network for Geospatial and Environmental Science (CHANGES) Research Center
description: Combines geographic information science, health data science, epidemiology and biomedical research to identify and predict gaps in health care, inform policy, and protect New Mexico communities from weather-related events and disasters.
notes: No funder or overall PI is named on the project page.

name: Extreme Weather, Natural Disasters and Impacts on Health Systems
description: Prototype GIS-based Climate-Related Disasters Risk Assessment and Projection System (C-DRAPS) to access data, assess risk and project health outcomes for disaster-affected populations, with a focus on rural areas.
team_sources: changes:Extreme Weather, Natural Disasters and Impacts on Health Systems

name: Linking Wildfire Smoke to Cancer
description: Links PM2.5 exposure estimates with cancer incidence and survival data to evaluate whether wildfire smoke contributes to cancer risk or poorer survival.

name: CHANGES Community Engagement Core
description: Builds capacity and partnerships through community-based participatory research: identifying community research priorities, co-developing communication strategies, and training in science communication and disaster preparedness.

name: CHANGES Data Core
description: Research infrastructure for data acquisition, processing, harmonization, analysis, synthesis, integration and dissemination across the CHANGES center.

name: CHANGES Community Engagement Work in Mora and San Miguel
description: Post-fire monitoring with communities downwind and downstream of the 2022 Hermit's Peak/Calf Canyon burn scar: a community air monitoring network and supplementary water-quality sampling for metals and organic compounds.
extent_label: Mora and San Miguel counties, New Mexico
notes: The point is the Mora County centroid (Nominatim); the work also covers San Miguel County. The page names no sites or team.

name: GC-AirWise: Grant County Air Information and Research for a Well-Informed Society
description: Community-based air quality monitoring with the Gila Resource Information Project (GRIP): 11 particulate-matter sensors across Grant County, cameras near mine sites, and a public dashboard.
notes: The point is the Grant County centroid (Nominatim); sensor locations are not published on the page. The page names no team.

name: FOR-NM: Forest Research for New Mexico Water and Carbon Management
description: Quantifies trade-offs among ecosystem water, carbon and watershed management in New Mexico forests, with research, K-12 education, workforce development and administrative cores.
funding_text: 4-year NSF-ERISE RII award (as worded on the project page)
extent_label: New Mexico (statewide); a collaboration between UNM, NMSU, WNMU, EMNRD, BEMP and Asombro
notes: The page names no study sites or watersheds.

name: Decentralized Water and Wastewater Systems in Rural Areas
description: Research on resilient, low-maintenance biofilm-based treatment (such as moving bed bioreactors) for small rural water and wastewater systems.
team_sources: pi:Decentralized Water and Wastewater Systems in Rural Areas

name: The Intermountain West Transformation Network
description: Partnership between UNM, seven other Western U.S. universities and more than 50 partner organizations on resilient headwaters, food-energy-water systems and governance across the Intermountain West.
notes: The page lists 'Melinda Morgan and additional team members', linking https://transformimw.unm.edu/team-members/ for the rest.

name: Public Perceptions of Potable Water Reuse
description: Public survey with the water utility (n=4000, 46% response rate) of Albuquerque residents' knowledge of local water issues and perceptions of water reuse.
extent_label: Albuquerque water utility service area, New Mexico
team_sources: pi:Public Perceptions of Potable Water Reuse
notes: The point is the Albuquerque city centroid (Nominatim), standing in for the utility service area.

name: Sevilleta Long-Term Ecological Research Program
description: Long-term study of how climate variability drives the dynamics of five dryland ecosystems, and the transitions among them, that converge at the Sevilleta National Wildlife Refuge.
extent_label: Sevilleta National Wildlife Refuge, central New Mexico
notes: The point is the refuge centroid (Nominatim).
